abstract: Abstract Galactinol synthase (GolS) catalyzes the first committed step in raffinose family oligosaccharide (RFO) biosynthesis and is implicated in plant adaptation to abiotic stress. However, for developing-world states, organised crime poses a far greater threat, undermining the rule of law and their monopoly on violence.

source: Crossref/Journal of Applied Meteorology and Climatology
abstract: Abstract Climate extremes have become increasingly frequent and severe worldwide under global warming. Among them, compound hot–dry events pose particularly acute threats to ecosystems, water resources, and agricultural systems, often producing greater impacts than heatwaves or droughts occurring alone. Using the ERA5-Land reanalysis dataset, we constructed a daily standardized compound dry and hot index (SCDHI) to investigate the spatiotemporal evolution of compound events across the Mongolian Plateau from 1995 to 2024.

AbstractThe impacts of the Madden-Julian Oscillation (MJO) on the monsoon season in South America (SA) and possible changes during El Niño (EN) and La Niña (LN) events are analyzed in the UK Met Office Unified Model Global Ocean Mixed Layer configuration (MetUM-GOML3). Experiments, with and without El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), are performed to assess if ENSO influences several MJO characteristics, including the teleconnections to SA. These experiments are sixty years long and consider different spatial resolutions.

AbstractThis study evaluates the performance of 74 CMIP6 (including HighResMIP) models for the historical climate of the Arabian Peninsula (AP). The analysis examines whether models reproduce the mean climate, trends (accounting internal-variability), extremes, and key circulation/process diagnostics. Despite strengths, several limitations persist across key aspects.

This study examines the political role of the Pakistan National Congress in the early phase of Pakistan (1947-1958). The PNC was one of the first organized groups of opposition in the first Constituent Assembly of Pakistan but it has been neglected in the historical narrative. Although the party had a representation in parliament, it started to have problems retaining its political influence in the newly founded state.

abstract: ABSTRACTA graphical abstract describes a concise, visual summary of a research paper's main findings. It presents the climate change and study methodology, hydro-climatic extremes and impacts, current adaptation responses and limitations, and recommendations/ way forward for climate-resilient WASH systems in Nepal. Climate change is intensifying hydro-climatic extremes across Nepal, triggering risks to water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) systems.

abstract: Growing evidence demonstrates the impact of health disparities on stroke care and outcomes. Although reviews have examined disparities related to sex and gender, race and ethnicity, socioeconomic status and rural–urban residence, most have not accounted for the influence of multiple intersecting social identities or positions. This critical integrative review used a modified integrative review methodology with an intersectionality approach.

Nevertheless, the identification of beneficial bacterial taxa that support plant resilience to environmental stresses and can be incorporated into synthetic microbial communities is still far from complete. Invasive alien (IA) predators can disrupt predator-prey interactions and alter prey phenotypes. However, how their effects differ from those of native predators remains poorly understood. Additionally, it is unclear to what extent these impacts interact with environmental factors such as warming and photoperiod.

Rising temperatures and extreme heat pose a substantial threat to human health through increases in heat-related morbidity and mortality. Moreover, social determinants of health can exacerbate the impact of heat on susceptible populations. This study investigates the inequities in heat-related emergency department (ED) visits in California from 2005-2017, focusing on how social determinants of health, represented by the California Healthy Places Index (HPI), may influence the associations between temperature and ED visits.

In this study, we produced green-synthesized zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO NPs) using leaves from Calotropis gigantea L. We assessed their effects on drought-stressed rough lemon (Citrus jambhiri L.) seedlings.

AbstractAs we move towards a green energy future, comprehensive site characterisation data for energy storage is critical for modelling, policy and guiding investment decisions. In this work, we present a dataset of 518 sub-surface formations spread across 34 countries with an emphasis on the under-explored Global South. Criteria relating to geological suitability and techno-economic feasibility from a wide range of data sources are collected from existing literature in a unified dataset.

PurposeThis article examines the strategic and ethical implications of regulatory arbitrage in global markets. While firms expand into less regulated environments to increase flexibility and growth, these strategies raise questions about long-term sustainability and corporate responsibility. The purpose is to show that regulatory arbitrage is not only a source of competitive advantage but also a potential source of strategic exposure, as actions taken in one market increasingly shape stakeholder perceptions across others.

Phase-change material (PCM) glazing and dynamic external shading are promoted as sustainable cooling measures, yet they act on the same solar load and are rarely assessed together under a mandatory energy code. This study aims to evaluate and compare the individual and combined performance of PCM glazing and adaptive external louvres in reducing cooling demand in a code-compliant office building under present and future hot–arid climates. The reference case is an SBC 601-compliant west-facing Riyadh office under present and 2080 weather.

ABSTRACTThis study introduces the ‘global forestation network’ (GFN)—an arrangement of actors that shape afforestation, reforestation, and forest restoration activities worldwide. These activities typically involve planting trees, and are motivated by supporting biodiversity, local communities, and climate change mitigation. At the GFN's core sit the ‘orchestrators’—the world's largest non‐governmental tree planting organisations—that collectively influence how forestation is financed and implemented.

The international economic interdependence and transnational organization of goods and services with global supply chains determine the economy, environment and working conditions in many countries around the world in numerous ways. The main risks in the supply chain are of an economic, ecological, political and ethical nature. The EU Supply Chain Act obliges companies to operate fairly and sustainably and to respect human rights and ecological protection in their supplier network.

ABSTRACTSince giraffe feeding practices have only been reported for European and US facilities, this study aimed to achieve a comprehensive overview of the current giraffe feeding practices on a global scale, as well as provide insights into the occurrence of oral stereotypies. We conducted a survey among zoos that house giraffes throughout the world. A total of 146 zoos responded and data on 702 individual giraffes were reported.
